newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Down with swaps, weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Down with swaps, weak demand.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices fell in line with swap quotes as weak fundamentals dragged prices lower, traders said on Thursday.
Late in the Asian trading day, a 20,000 tonne cargo lifting July 14-18 was traded at the $100 per tonne mark, lower than the previous $101.50 traded on Wednesday.
Traders said offers outnumbered bids. At least four sellers emerged to offer cargoes lifting July 4-19 at $100-$101 per tonne. Only two bids were indicated at $99-$100 per tonne.
They said demand remained weak.
South Korean exports in July are higher than those in June as most refiners are already back onstream after their recent maintenance shutdowns.
The market was also waiting for the results of Taiwan's fuel oil import tender for 38,000 tonnes which is expected tobe awarded on Friday.

KEPCO has awarded three cargoes of fuel oil to Dutch tradre Vitol in its tender which closed today. A 74,000 tonne cargo each for August 13-17, August 28-Sept 1 and Sept 18-22 was awarded at $123.93/T for the first two cargoes and the third cargo at $121.95.
KEPCO last bought two 70,000-tonne, 540-cst cargo at $126.70 and $133.00 per tonne respectively.
The swaps market was talked down, with July last quoted at $98.50/$99.00 against Wednesday's $99.25/$99.75. August swaps were quoted at $97.75/$98.25 against $98.25/$99.00.
Traders said Indonesia were expected expected to award between 2.5 and 3.0 million barrels of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) in July.
LSWR prices were expected to rise after hovering around just above the $15.00-per-barrel mark in recent weeks.
Traders said prices would be supported by firmer demand from Japan as the summer season neared and a smaller allocation from Indonesia, traders said.
The reduced allocation is due to the shutdown of the Balongan refinery in Indonesia starting July 10. MTH FOB SIN BUY/SELL PREV BUY/SELL
